extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors, broadcasters, and general readers interested in wartime policy
extracted.subtask_description: A wartime newspaper page reporting policy changes, censorship guidance, and government recommendations about production, manpower, taxes and public-order measures; useful for editors and broadcasters deciding what to publish and for merchants and officials implementing controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Censorship restriction on POW reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Censorship requests that nothing be published or broadcast about the arrival, movements, or confinements of prisoners of war brought to this country, except on the authority of the provost marshal general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only material authorized by the provost marshal general (responsible for security and treatment) may be published or broadcast; emphasizes provisions of international law and the privacy/maintenance rights of prisoners and that the rule protects American prisoners abroad as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merchants' permissible inventory limits (WPB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the War Production Board order, no merchant will be permitted to keep in stock any larger ratio of merchandise to his sales in any quarter of the year than he had on hand in the average of the comparable quarters in 1939, 1940 and 1941.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms instructing merchants on details for determining permissible inventories will be made available; the order applies to inventories of finished consumers' goods and is part of a program for formal control and enforcement of normal inventories.

rubrics_metrics.name: WPB control and enforcement of normal inventories
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Production Board will proceed to formal control and enforcement of inventories of finished consumers' goods to prevent hoarding and to achieve desired wartime distribution results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is described as a second-step program after initial reporting—WPB will issue orders, set permissible inventory ratios (see merchant rule), and provide forms and instructions to wholesale and retail firms for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to create Office of War Mobilization (centralize wartime agencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: A congressional committee recommended creating a new super agency — the Office of War Mobilization — to subordinate and coordinate WPB, War Manpower Commission/Selective Service Administration duties, and the Office of Price Administration (as Office of War Mobilization's chief branch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested structure: an Office of War Supply (taking procurement functions), an Office of War Manpower (taking War Manpower Commission and Selective Service duties), and an Office of Economic Stabilization (operating agency where OPA would be chief); rationale: end hoarding, streamline production, and eliminate 'business-as-usual' considerations in wartime agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use occupational deferment as primary instrument for manpower organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee recommends that 'occupational deferment must become the chief instrument for organizing our manpower supply' and that the nation's manpower be used 'where it will be most useful in winning the war.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy would precede service legislation; implies deferment decisions should prioritize war production needs over blanket legislative labor apportionment and recognizes regional/time variation in labor conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective restrictions proposed for 18- and 19-year-old draftees
rubrics_metrics.description: There is movement in the Senate to surround the proposed military draft of 18- and 19-year-old men with protective restrictions for their schooling, training and off-duty activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters and petitions from mothers and organizations urged protections including insulating Army camps against liquor and vice; the House bill contains provisions to allow high school and college students to finish their academic year (a provision several Senators wanted in the Senate measure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Victory tax and payroll deduction provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The tax bill imposes a new 'victory tax' and establishes payroll deductions to begin Jan. 1; 'all individuals will be taxed a flat five per cent' (as described on the page) with payroll deductions for the victory tax commencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payroll deductions are permitted for debt payments, insurance premiums and war bond purchases (or a portion of the tax may be recovered later); the bill included other income tax increases and surtaxes described elsewhere on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income and corporate tax changes including excess-profits tax rise
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill raises normal individual income tax rates (noted increase from 4% to 6% on normal rate and addition of graduated surtax), lowers personal exemptions, and raises excess-profits taxes — described as being taxed at 90% after a $5,000 exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resulting structure (as reported) leads to higher effective tax burdens across income levels; congressional leaders anticipated further tax measures and noted the combined effect of new and existing levies would represent a substantial portion of national income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calls to insulate Army camps from liquor and vice
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions and letters urged that Army camps be insulated against liquor and vice and that restrictions/regulations be imposed on and near military posts to protect inducted youths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was cited as part of broader 'protective restrictions' discussions for young draftees; senators and organizations pressed for measures to control intoxicating liquors and vice near military installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism of WPB devolution and need to convert WPB to wartime production role
rubrics_metrics.description: Congressional committee criticized the War Production Board for permitting devolution of responsibilities to military agencies and 'endless jockeying' between branches; recommended WPB be converted to the job of war production with clearer, centralized authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee cited failures like hoarding, improper utilization of skills, patchwork methods and lack of a national production program; the recommendation supports reassigning procurement and policy authority to a super agency to avoid collisions between production projects.
